packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET packet-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (isolated first reader)

EXPOSURE STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification, author, title or earlier
reading of this item. I have not tried to identify the work. Everything below is read
from the supplied images only.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
======================================================================
Four overviews = four faces of what looks like two parchment leaves mounted on paper
guards in a modern binding:
  image-001  Face A. Modern numeral "104" top right. Single column, long lines, c. 41 lines.
  image-010  Face B. No numeral. Single column, long lines, c. 41 lines. Shown again as the
             left half of image-019, facing Face C (so B and C form one opening).
  image-019  Face C (right half). Modern numeral "105" top right. Single column, c. 41 lines.
  image-028  Face D. Single column, c. 41 lines; round red/orange ink stamp in the left
             margin overlapping the start of lines c. 19-24 (stamp legend not legible to me).

Observations
- Orientation upright on all faces. No running titles seen. No ruling-frame commentary,
  no interlinear gloss; a few small interlinear corrections/insertions only.
- Faces A and B: small, heavily abbreviated bookhand in brown ink; each new item opens with
  a red one-line initial (plain red capitals C, Y, E, C, A on A; G, L, L, A, C, S, T, C, A, C,
  B, O, G, Y, L, E, C, A, S, S, O, O on B). On A the items mostly start a new line; on B the
  red initials mostly stand inside the line (run-on items). No rubric titles.
- Faces C and D: similar small script, browner/paler ink, NO red initials. Items are
  introduced by a brown paraph/bracket sign and a heading that is underlined (and sometimes
  boxed) in ink, e.g. "Ad ...", "Item ad ...", "Unguentum ad ...", "Elact...". Run-on layout.
- Face D left margin: a marginal note in the text ink beside line 7, underlined,
  reading "de glandulis"; a fainter marginal note lower down (beside lines c. 11-12)
  that I cannot read; further faint marks near the lower left corner.
- Damage: both leaves are darkened and rubbed, worst along the top third of A and B and the
  outer margin of A; several holes; a cockled/creased lower outer corner on C/D; a tear
  through the lower centre of A and B. Paper/tissue repairs at lower corners.
Tentative interpretation (not observation): A-B read as a run of short entries on single
drugs that purge named humours; C-D read as a collection of short recipes arranged by
complaint. Whether the two leaves were adjacent in the original book cannot be told from
these images; text does not obviously run on from B to C.

======================================================================
2. CONVENTIONS
======================================================================
- Each physical line is labelled with the face line number (A1, A2 ...) and then the tile(s)
  and tile line number counted from the top of that tile, e.g. [002:5 | 003:5] = left part
  read in image-002 line 5, right part in image-003 line 5. A clipped first line of a tile is
  counted as line 1, so tile line numbers may be off by one in places.
- Tiles overlap: 002/003 with 004/005, 004/005 with 006/007, 006/007 with 008/009 (and the
  same pattern on the other faces). Repeated lines are given once.
- (..) = my expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain reading;
  [illegible] = not read; [..] = short gap. (et) = Tironian et. ℈ = the scruple-like sign,
  ʒ = the drachm-like sign, ℥ = the ounce-like sign (the signs are hard to tell apart here
  and all three are uncertain throughout). Numerals as written.
- RED: marks a red initial.

======================================================================

7. LIMITATIONS AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
======================================================================
- This is an unverified image reading. Abbreviation expansions in parentheses are mine.
  Weight signs (scruple / drachm / ounce) and small numerals are frequently uncertain.
- Drug names are transcribed as I see the letters; several are doubtful and marked with ?
  (e.g. A29 "Ysion", A33 "Elacteri", A35 "Cocognidium", B2 "Gnicus", B4 "Lacterides",
  B11 "Scorax", B17 "Alna" and "Camepitheos", B18 "Bdellui", B20 "Olibani", B24 "Lepidos
  calcis", B30 "Camelea", B34 "Amoniaci thimiamatos", C10 "Seralogodion"/"Generusium",
  C36 "Theod... ypotilon", D13 "Diamoron barinum", D21 heading after "Elact").
  I did not normalise them to dictionary forms.
- Largely unread or fragmentary: Face A lines 1-4 and 9-16; Face B lines 5-12 (left half);
  Face C lines 4-8 and the right-hand ends of 33-41 (creased corner); Face D lines 1-7,
  22-32 and the faint marginal note beside lines 11-12; the legend of the red stamp on D.
- Line counts per face (c. 41) are my count from tiles and may be off by one where a rubbed
  line is hard to separate from its neighbour; tile line numbers inherit that.
- Column order is not in doubt (single column on every face). Leaf order is taken from the
  modern numerals 104 / 105; I cannot tell from the images whether B-C were consecutive in
  the original book or whether C continues B.
- A raking-light or multispectral image of the top third of A and B, and a flattened shot of
  the lower outer corner of C/D, would be the most useful additional views.
